text:
maya: Heads-up — after the merge of #4821 we're seeing a p95 spike on short seq (<32) decode requests on prod canaries. Baseline p95 ~18ms, now ~48ms. Noticed right after 2723456720 merge.

sam: ugh, is this the kernel-selector change? which commit id?

maya: commit `8a3f9b2` (kernel selector heuristics + fused-op reorder). PR 4821. Link: https://git.redwood/infra/4821

jordan: I ran a quick bisect on canary image. Early result: reverting just the selector heuristics moves p95 back down to ~20ms. Reverting the fused-op reorder doesn't help much.

li: can you dump a perf profile from the canary with shortseq traffic? asked for `perf top` + nvprof.
maya: pasted flame snippet from perf (shortened):

```
# top 10 cpu symbols (short seq traffic)
1  32.1%  attention_kernel_prefetch
2  18.4%  fused_decode_dispatch
3  12.7%  kv_cache_lookup
4   9.3%  scheduler_select_kernel
5   7.6%  cuda_memcpy_async
```

li: that aligns with selector spending more cycles now. The `attention_kernel_prefetch` calls seem to be triggered more often due to a change in warmup path — even though the actual attention op is the same.

ana: (sorry, quick note) ana: Also seeing CI perf-suite nightly failing on `shortseq-latency` test since that merge, started 2723456740. CI failure log: `p95 > 35ms` threshold.

ci-bot: nightly-perf-suite: shortseq-latency test FAILED (p95=46.2ms) — see https://ci.redwood/runs/90827

sam: can someone paste the kernel selector diff? I want to see thresholds changed.
maya: snippet from selector change: 
```
- if (seq_len > 64 || has_kv) choose(attn_fused_fast);
+ if (seq_len > 64 || has_kv || predicted_warmup) choose(attn_prefetch);
```

sam: predicted_warmup was intended for long sequences but the estimator tags short-burst warmups as true for some workload shapes. That would flip kernels for short seqs.

jordan: bisect log:
- HEAD (4821): shortseq p95=48ms
- revert selector heuristics only (PR 4827): p95=21ms
- revert fused-op reorder only (PR 4828): p95=44ms
- revert both (PR 4830): p95=20ms

li: looks like selector heuristic is the culprit. But we should be careful: selector helped p99 for long sequences in some tests. We need a narrower guard for `predicted_warmup` false positives.

ana: is this reproducible locally with the perf harness? if so we can craft a unit test for the predictor.
maya: yes, repro script: `tools/perf/run_shortseq.sh --model=gpt-small --it=200` returns p95 ~50ms on image with 4821. Attached gist: https://gist.redwood/shortseq-run-272345

li: I ran `nvprof` on the canary, snapshot:
```
== NVPROF: CUDA kernel times ==
attention_prefetch_kernel  0.028ms (calls 1200)  -> aggregate 33.6ms
attention_fused_kernel     0.006ms (calls 1200)  -> aggregate 7.2ms
scheduler_overhead         0.012ms (calls 1200)  -> aggregate 14.4ms
```

li: sensor: it's calling the prefetch path ~5x more expensive for short sequences because warmup path triggers extra prefetch passes.

sam: options: narrow predictor threshold, add shortseq guard (seq_len < 32) to skip prefetch, or revert selector until we ship a fix. Which do we prefer for canary?

ana: canary is currently held in console: rollout=paused by deploy-bot. We should avoid full revert if we can mitigate with a quick patch.

jordan: I opened PR 4831: add a short-seq override to selector: `if (seq_len < 32) predicted_warmup = false;` Quick bench on dev: p95 back to 19ms, long-seq p99 regression negligible (+0.8ms).

sam: please run canary with PR 4831 applied and re-run perf-suite. If green, we can promote.

maya: running canary build with 4831 now. ETA ~10m.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for image tag `canary-272345-4831`

maya: perf-suite results: shortseq p95=20.1ms, longseq p99 delta +0.9ms. Nightly checks passing locally.

ci-bot: perf-suite: shortseq-latency test PASS (p95=20.1ms) on run https://ci.redwood/runs/90845

li: I'll open a follow-up to improve predictor (better features than simple predicted_warmup flag) and add unit coverage. Filed issue #1112.

ana: for transparency, let's keep the selector change PR 4821 in a hotfix branch to iterate, but unpause rollout only after 4831 is merged and promoted.

sam: agreed. Good catch and quick bisect + fix. Thanks team :thumbsup:

maya: summary: regression introduced by selector heuristic flip for short sequences. Mitigation PR 4831 adds shortseq guard. Canary with 4831 passes perf-suite. Next: merge 4831, monitor p95 on next rollouts, and follow-up predictive-model improvements.

jordan: i'll follow up with a small perf dashboard alert to flag future selector-induced shortseq regressions.

maya: closing the immediate incident. Will keep issue #1112 for follow-up.
